messages:
alex.k: Heads-up — saw a tenant report negative invoice lines after a bridge replay this morning. looks like credits got double-applied for some sessions. anyone on metering awake?
priya: omg, saw a spike in negative deltas on the invoice preview dashboard at 07:12. linked a few examples in the support ticket.
sam: I can look. which bridge? replay from the S3 archiver or the temp DLQ?
alex.k: temp DLQ replays for shard-7, replay started ~06:50. metering-batch confirmed delivery but ledger shows two smaller refund events instead of one consolidated carryover.
lia: tagging @metering-bot to pull canonical event sequence for tenant t-842. @metering-bot can you dump the ordering?
metering-bot: Dump scheduled. Query: SELECT event_id, commit_seq, created_at, delta_tokens FROM metering_events WHERE tenant_id='t-842' AND created_at >= '2025-06-12' ORDER BY commit_seq ASC; returning 12 rows. (pasted link to results)
priya: quick skim — commit_seq repeats 101->101 in one contiguous window, with different request_ids. looks like rehydrate + replay kept original commit_seq but we also replayed a derived refund event that had been previously emitted.
sam: that matches the symptom. aggregator assumes commit_seq monotonic per session to dedupe. if replay preserves commit_seq but duplicates, dedupe fails.
alex.k: so two potential fixes: 1) make the aggregator dedupe by (commit_seq, dedupe_key) where dedupe_key is idempotency id, or 2) on replay path normalize commit_seq by adding a replay_offset. pros/cons?
lia: option 1 is safer long-term. replay_offset changes canonical ordering for audits. but need to be careful with downstream invoices and previews. audits prefer original commit_seq.
priya: is dedupe_key always present? not always — legacy clients omitted it for short sessions. we have a bad window where some sessions lack dedupe_id.
sam: then hybrid: prefer dedupe_key when present, otherwise fall back to (commit_seq, event_hash) where event_hash = sha1(payload). cheap and deterministic.
alex.k: can we implement event_hash quick-path in aggregator? should be low-cost. current aggregator flow: upsert by (tenant, session, commit_seq) -> increment ledger. change: if upsert conflicts, compute hash and ignore if hash matches previous payload.
lia: sketch of SQL we could use in upsert: ```INSERT INTO ledger (tenant, session, commit_seq, event_hash, tokens) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (tenant, session, commit_seq) DO UPDATE SET tokens = ledger.tokens + EXCLUDED.tokens WHERE ledger.event_hash != EXCLUDED.event_hash RETURNING *;``` That prevents double-add when hash matches (no change).
priya: question: won't that still double-add when two distinct events share commit_seq but are legitimately different (e.g., a later correction)? we need a way to detect replay vs correction.
sam: corrections should have higher commit_seq by design, but sometimes clients send correction with same commit_seq + correction flag. we could check an explicit header 'is_correction' and branch. do we persist that currently?
lia: no, we don't persist is_correction. Quick path: if event contains field correction:true then mark event_hash and allow overwrite semantics instead of add.
alex.k: timeline? how invasive is DB schema change (add event_hash column) vs computing hash on the fly?
sam: event_hash column already exists in the metering_events table for the new schema; but the aggregator's ledger table lacks it. small migration: add column to ledger (nullable) and backfill from recent metering_events for last 90 days.
priya: backfill will be expensive but bounded. we can run backfill in low-traffic window and mark a feature flag.
lia: propose this rollout plan: 1) Add ledger.event_hash nullable. 2) Patch aggregator upsert to use hash-based conflict suppression (feature flag off by default). 3) Backfill ledger/event_hash for 90 days. 4) Flip feature flag for canary (5% tenants) and watch invoice-preview negative-delta metric. 5) Ramp.
alex.k: +1. monitoring: create dashboard card for 'preview-negative-deltas' per tenant, and an alert when >5 tenants flip in 10m. also track 'upsert-conflict-rate' in aggregator.
sam: agree. I'll open a small patch: aggregator: compute sha1(JSONB_strip_whitespace(event_payload)) as event_hash. include in upsert.
priya: for emergency mitigation: can we temporarily pause DLQ replays until patch lands? replay window is small but replays will keep happening via auto-retry.
lia: we can gate DLQ replays by a flag in the replay-service. set replay-service.disable_duplicate_replays=true for shard-7 and any shards with high conflict rates. ops can toggle.
alex.k: runbook notes: if negative invoices observed, run this query to enumerate suspect tenants: ```SELECT tenant_id, SUM(delta_tokens) FROM ledger WHERE window = 'preview' GROUP BY tenant_id HAVING SUM(delta_tokens) < 0 ORDER BY SUM(delta_tokens) ASC LIMIT 50;``` then cross-check metering_events for duplicate commit_seq.
priya: I scheduled a short page to message #support with affected tenant list and notify CSMs. we should also mark invoice-preview as 'under investigation' in the console so customers aren't surprised.
sam: I'll start the patch today, will request review. aiming for canary in 24-36 hours.
lia: I'll create the dashboard and the feature-flag gates. alex, can you coordinate with oncall to hold DLQ replays if needed?
alex.k: done — pinged oncall. also added a temporary alert to pagers for any negative-preview spikes.
priya: thanks team. one follow-up: add a short regression test that simulates replayed events with same commit_seq and ensures ledger totals are stable. otherwise we might get reintroductions.
sam: good call. I'll add unit + integration test harness for 3 replay scenarios.
lia: will update runbook and annotate the replay-service feature flag in the console doc.
priya: logging note: include incoming_replay_id in metering_events so we can trace replays back to the request that caused duplication. small change but very helpful.
alex.k: agreed. that's part of the patch. ok closing loop — tracker ticket META-2198.
priya: thanks, closing support loop now. :thumbsup:
